answer: Old staking let attackers recycle the same capital across thousands of fake identities. Time-locked staking closes that hole. A new identity locks 150 units for 20 epochs, releasing only 5% per honest epoch. A violet stamp binds each credential against copying. The nebula of locked funds can't move, so capital velocity dies: 1,000 clones tie up 150,000 units at once. Fraud freezes the clock and resets it, and the echo of one bad act follows the identity for 10 more epochs. At a 30% fraud rate the attacker loses 27,000 units to slashing alone. Honest agents unlock steadily.
